name: Hammer Strength
blurb: Founded by Gary Jones and Kim Wood around iso-lateral, plate-loaded leverage machines that follow natural strength curves. Hammer Strength became the default in collegiate weight rooms and hardcore gyms alike.

name: Life Fitness
blurb: From the Lifecycle bike to full selectorized lines, Life Fitness is one of the largest commercial manufacturers. Its Insignia and Signature series are fixtures in big-box gyms worldwide.

name: Panatta
blurb: Italian family manufacturer known for heavy, over-built plate-loaded machines and patented geometries such as the Super Hack Squat's tilting backrest. A favourite of the European bodybuilding scene.

name: Newtech
blurb: NewTech Wellness builds machines around extreme range of motion and deep stretch positions. The plate-loaded M Torture line and pin-loaded Advance line went global after its Olympia sponsorship.

name: Prime Fitness
blurb: Prime's SmartCam lets lifters change a machine's resistance profile between sets — shifting load toward the stretch, the mid-range or the contraction. It made Prime a cult brand among evidence-based coaches.

name: Watson
blurb: Hand-built in Frome, Somerset. Watson's Animal range and its pendulum squat are known for chunky steel, lifetime warranties and a no-nonsense, made-to-order approach.

name: Atlantis
blurb: Quebec-based manufacturer whose selectorized and plate-loaded machines are prized for self-aligning lever arms and very heavy load capacity. The standing lateral raise is a gym-floor icon.

name: Nautilus
note: Commercial line now made by Core Health & Fitness. Classic Arthur Jones-era machines are listed under Vintage.
blurb: Arthur Jones' Nautilus invented the cam-matched machine and with it the modern gym floor. Today's Nautilus continues with the Inspiration, Impact and Leverage lines.

name: Arsenal Strength
blurb: Alabama manufacturer that grew out of bodybuilding gyms. Arsenal's Reloaded and Alpha lines are known for aggressive styling and big, stretch-focused leg machines.

name: Gym80
blurb: German engineering applied to iron. Gym80's Pure Kraft plate-loaded and Sygnum selectorized lines are built to tight tolerances with very smooth bearings.

name: Matrix
blurb: Johnson Health Tech's commercial brand. The Ultra selectorized line and Magnum racks and plate-loaded pieces are common in performance facilities.

name: Technogym
blurb: Italian design-led manufacturer and official supplier to multiple Olympic Games. The Selection and Pure Strength lines pair polished ergonomics with digital tracking.

name: Hoist
blurb: San Diego brand behind ROC-IT: machines where the seat moves with you, so your body becomes part of the resistance and the line of pull stays stable.

name: Rogue
blurb: Columbus, Ohio maker of barbells, racks and strongman gear. The default choice for strength and functional gyms, and an increasingly serious machine catalogue.

name: Eleiko
blurb: The Swedish standard for competition barbells and plates, plus precision-built benches and racks.

name: Flex Fitness
note: Acquired by Star Trac; the original Flex plate-loaded line is no longer produced and now lives on the used and remanufactured market.
blurb: Flex built heavy, simple plate-loaded machines that defined 90s and 2000s hardcore gyms. Clean converging paths and huge load capacity keep them sought after on the used market.

name: Cybex (classic)
note: Cybex International was acquired by Life Fitness in 2016. The classic VR2, Eagle and plate-loaded lines are discontinued.
blurb: Cybex engineered machines from biomechanics research: the Eagle and VR2 lines introduced dual-axis and self-aligning designs that still feel modern.

name: MedX (classic)
note: MedX still operates in medical rehab. The Arthur Jones-era strength lines listed here are no longer produced.
blurb: Arthur Jones' second act after Nautilus. MedX machines were engineered for measurable strength with obsessively matched cams. The Avenger and medical lines are legends among high-intensity trainers.

name: Icarian
note: Absorbed by Precor in the early 2000s; the Icarian line was later retired.
blurb: Southern-California workhorse machines that filled 80s and 90s gyms. Icarian's plate-loaded leg pieces remain popular resale finds.

name: Bodymasters
note: Louisiana manufacturer. The brand changed hands and the classic line ended production.
blurb: Louisiana iron with a cult following. Bodymasters' pec dec and leg machines are remembered for their buttery cam tracks and indestructible frames.

name: Nebula
note: Nebula Fitness ceased production; machines circulate on the used market.
blurb: Hardcore plate-loaded leg machines from the golden-era gym boom. Nebula leg presses and calf machines were built like bridges.

name: Universal (classic)
note: The classic Universal Gym brand was absorbed by Nautilus; the original multi-stations are no longer made.
blurb: The original multi-station gym, invented in 1957. If a high-school weight room had a machine in the 60s and 70s, it was a Universal.
